lead.title: Cardiovalve meets its endpoints in the TARGET trial and readies its transcatheter tricuspid valve for Europe
lead.deck: Presented on Nov. 22 as a late-breaker at PCR London Valves by Prof. Georg Nickenig (Bonn University Hospital), six-month full-cohort data from TARGET (157 patients enrolled, 148 implanted, mean age 78, nearly 40% with torrential tricuspid regurgitation) met both 30-day primary endpoints, performance and safety; 76.9% of patients had no or trace regurgitation at three years, and the enhanced delivery system cut major bleeding from 21% to 5%. The Venus Medtech subsidiary has filed for CE marking and targets EU commercialization in the second half of 2027: a new challenger to Edwards' EVOQUE, the only orthotopic transcatheter tricuspid valve sold in Europe.

milestone.title: Anteris' 'biomimetic' DurAVR aortic valve posts 1% heart failure hospitalization at one year in small annuli
milestone.summary: In 100 patients with severe aortic stenosis and small aortic annuli, pooled from the EMBARK and early feasibility studies in the US and Europe, the single-leaflet DurAVR transcatheter valve showed at one year a mean gradient of 8.9 mmHg (down from 48.1 mmHg before implant), no moderate or severe paravalvular leak, no valve-related deaths (all-cause mortality 6%) and 1% heart failure hospitalization; data presented on Nov. 22 at PCR London Valves by Rishi Puri (Cleveland Clinic).
milestone.why: Small annuli, common in women, are the weak spot of current TAVI valves (poor hemodynamics, patient-prosthesis mismatch). Anteris now tests its thesis in PARADIGM, a randomized pivotal trial of about 1,000 patients, head to head against commercial valves, enrolling in the US and Europe: a real-world test of whether a challenger can still shake up the Edwards-Medtronic duopoly.

brefsEurope.title: UK health department wants to cut DTAC assessment of digital technologies 'from months to days'
brefsEurope.summary: David Lawson, DHSC's director of medical technology, laid out the roadmap: a digital system surfacing information on all medical devices is partly launching (webinars in December), a workflow assurance tool is due in spring 2027 to avoid repeated submissions, and completion targets will be set for local risk checks. For medtechs, the prize is faster NHS access, with average DTAC lead times above 12 weeks according to an ABHI survey.

brefsIntl.title: Ladera Medical presents full FASTEN results for its large-bore arterial closure system
brefsIntl.summary: In 55 transfemoral TAVI patients at six sites in Australia, Belgium and the Netherlands, the device achieved 98.1% freedom from major access-site complications at 30 days and hemostasis in 0.5 minutes on average (late-breaker at London Valves, presented by Jan van der Heyden, Sint-Jan Hospital Bruges). The device remains investigational and is not for sale anywhere: a startup to watch ahead of its next regulatory step.

word.definition: An artificial heart valve, folded inside a catheter threaded through a vein in the leg or neck, is deployed in place of the leaking tricuspid valve, without opening the chest or stopping the heart.

parts.label: Self-expanding frame
parts.role: anchoring in the native annulus and leaflets

parts.label: Delivery system
parts.role: transport via the femoral or jugular vein

how.t: ECG-gated CT measures the tricuspid annulus and simulates implantation; transesophageal echo assesses the regurgitation, right-ventricular function and any pacemaker leads.
Through a femoral vein, the team advances a guidewire into the right ventricle, then pushes the large-bore delivery system across the annulus under transesophageal echo guidance.
The valve is released on the ventricular side, its anchors grasp the native leaflets, then it is released on the atrial side; for EVOQUE, deployment takes about 30 minutes.

word.why: Tricuspid regurgitation, long the 'forgotten valve', mostly affects elderly patients too frail for surgery. Replacement removes the leak more predictably than edge-to-edge repair (about 95% at most mild regurgitation at one year, versus about 50%), but at the cost of more pacemakers (28% vs 4% in TRISCEND II) and annuli sometimes too large for current valves. With Edwards' EVOQUE the only orthotopic valve sold in Europe, the race is on: TRiCares' European and US pivotal trials, VDyne's head-to-head against EVOQUE, Cardiovalve's CE filing — and as many potential targets for the majors.

startups.name: TRiCares
startups.use: Topaz valve; TRICURE pivotal trial in Europe and US IDE pivotal trial started in July 2026; €20M EIB loan in January 2026 after a $50M Series D

startups.name: VDyne
startups.use: Side-delivered, annulus-anchored TriNova valve; randomized TRIVITA pivotal trial against EVOQUE (up to 70 sites in the US and Europe), first patient treated in July 2026

startups.name: Trisol Medical
startups.use: Dome-shaped tricuspid valve implanted via jugular then femoral access; US feasibility study published in EuroIntervention in November 2026 (94.7% technical success)
